text:
support-alex: FYI Cerulean is seeing intermittent 429s and a few 503s from their dedicated pool in us-west-2 starting ~03:50 UTC. Customer says auth errors + billing jump. Opening thread to triage.

deploy-bot: alert: cerulean-prod-pool-usw2 high 429 rate (15m avg) -> 03:50:12Z. autoscale_event: none. recent deploy: none.

sre-ryan: can someone paste Cerulean's baseline/peak QPS and whether their min_replicas was >0? also did autoscaler report any activity in that window?

cs-talya: Cerulean report: baseline ~60 QPS, typical peaks ~320 QPS, but had a campaign burst hitting ~1,100 QPS for ~7 minutes. They also had a token rotation that briefly spiked auth calls. min_replicas for their pool was 1.

eng-diego: quick hypothesis: pool was undersized + cold KV cache warmup. Our autoscaler is currently CPU-based; workload is GPU/token-bound so CPU stayed low and autoscaler didn't kick. that explains no autoscale_event.

infra-jess: checking config: their dedicated pool config: {"min_replicas":1, "max_replicas":8, "target_utilization_pct":70, "scale_metric":"cpu"}. Agree this metric mismatch could delay scale-up during token-heavy bursts.

sre-ryan: logs show queue_length spikes and auth 401 retries from customer client -> client retried aggressively which amplified QPS. Also saw increased token generation cost in billing metrics.

cs-talya: customer is worried about billing — they got surge charges during the burst. They want a short-term remediation and a longer-term sizing plan.

eng-diego: short-term mitigation options:
- bump min_replicas to 3 for immediate headroom
- add a warmup job that floods a few warm requests to populate KV cache on failover
- change autoscaler to use queue_length or gpu_util/token_rate in addition to CPU

infra-jess: proposed quick plan we can do in next 30m:
1) update pool min_replicas:1->3 (impacts cost, reduces cold throttles)
2) apply a temporary autoscaler policy: add metric queue_length scale-up rule
3) run controlled warmup script against pool (5rps for 60s)

eng-diego: longer-term sizing calc (back-of-envelope):
- Cerulean peak observed 1100 QPS, average request ~25 tokens, target utilization 50% to absorb spikes.
- Our per-GPU sustained throughput for this model ~= 2000 tokens/sec (est). so tokens/sec at peak = 1100 * 25 = 27,500 tps -> GPUs needed = ceil(27,500 / (2000 * 0.5)) = ceil(27,500 / 1000) = 28 GPUs. that seems high because requests are short; using more realistic per-GPU concurrency (batching) brings it down.
- alternate estimate using QPS capacity: if one GPU can handle ~120 QPS at 50% util -> GPUs = ceil(1100 / 120) = 10 GPUs.
Recommendation: increase pool to 10 GPUs reserved (or equivalent vCPU/GPU units) and set min_replicas to 4 for warm headroom. target_utilization 45-55%.

cs-talya: customer prefers to avoid a big immediate commit. they'd accept a staged approach: short-term bump to 3 replicas + autoscaler tweak, then monitor for 48 hours before committing to a 10-GPU reserved slab.

sre-ryan: I'll run a repro script to emulate burst and auth rotation to validate autoscaler change. repro steps below (use internal test token):
```
# emulate Cerulean burst
for i in $(seq 1 1200); do
  curl -s -X POST https://inference.redwood.ai/v1/gen \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer TEST-ROTATE-TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"openchat-small","input":"ping","max_tokens":20}' &
done
wait
```
Note: include auth rotation by swapping header token after 200 requests to simulate their client.

infra-jess: I'll push the min_replicas change and add queue_length rule. rolling change will take ~5m; warmup script then. I'll annotate deploy and cost impact in the change doc.

support-alex: good. can we also add an alert rule for queue_length 1min > 200 to avoid surprise next time?

eng-diego: yes, add alert and a dashboard tile showing token/sec, gpu_util, queue_length, and autoscale_actions. I'll add an annotation to the rollout: "cerulean warmup intervention".

cs-talya: I'll message Cerulean with the staged plan and expected timeline: min_replicas bump now, monitor 48h, then propose reserved capacity if spikes persist.

sre-ryan: will run repro and post results here. if repro shows autoscaler still slow we can try direct scale-up to 6 GPUs as intermediate step.

support-alex: thanks all. tagging @cs-talya to keep customer notified. I'll close the incident thread once we confirm 48h monitoring started.

deploy-bot: change accepted: pool config update queued by infra-jess. estimated cost delta: +~1.8x for next 24h at min_replicas=3.

sre-ryan: repro run in progress, posting findings shortly. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
